title: 1.1.18 Same Framework, Different Weight
description: Five multiple-choice questions on the four Ps and why two teams elaborate the same framework differently. Checked instantly.

questions.question: What are the four Ps?
questions.explanation: Problem, project, people, product. They are the four factors a framework gets elaborated around.

questions.question: What are the four framework activities, in order?
questions.explanation: Inception, elaboration, construction, deployment — the book's names. The five-phase list in the 1.1.5 video (design, development, testing, deployment, maintenance) is the same lifecycle under industry names.

questions.question: Two teams follow the same four framework activities but work very differently. What explains the difference?
options: The four Ps differ between the projects, so each activity gets more or less weight
One team skips activities the other performs
The activities mean different things at different companies
They are writing in different programming languages
questions.explanation: Both teams keep all four activities. The four Ps decide how much weight each one carries.

questions.question: A small team builds an app for one school. A large team builds a banking system for thousands of customers. Which project gets the heavier elaboration, and why?
options: The school app — schools have stricter rules about software
Neither — the framework fixes how much work each activity gets
The banking system — banking software is written in more programming languages
The banking system — the product has to be reliable for thousands of people, so the phases carry more weight
questions.explanation: Same four activities, heavier elaboration. The product and the people it serves are what raise the stakes.

questions.question: Which of the four Ps is about who does the work?
questions.explanation: People. Problem is how hard the work is, project is how it is managed, product is what gets built.
